intro: Week 8 ended with the Vikings losing their first game and the Ravens losing their quarterback to a thumb injury. Cardinals, Bengals and Buccaneers all turned in games nobody saw coming, and Bears at Seahawks closes the week tonight. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Lions end the Vikings' unbeaten run with a 19-15 win
top.dek: Jared Goff hit Jameson Williams in the back of the end zone to put Detroit ahead after the Lions trailed 15-12. Detroit moved to 5-2 and 2-0 in the division, and Minnesota took its first loss at 6-1. The Lions defense then forced a three-and-out to seal it.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Lamar Jackson heads to injured reserve with a thumb injury
top.dek: Jackson hurt his right thumb on the first snap of his return against Buffalo and will have surgery. He must miss at least four games, and coach Jesse Minter did not rule out a season-ending result. Backup Tyler Huntley is out with a toe injury too, and Baltimore sits at 4-4 after three straight losses.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Tyler Allgeier runs for 147 yards on 11 carries in Dallas
top.dek: Allgeier broke a 63-yard touchdown on Gardner Minshew's second snap and added five catches for 44 yards and a score. With the other Arizona backs hurt, he carried the backfield down the stretch of a 33-30 overtime win.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 1,098: unique final scores in NFL history, with 43-36 the newest
top.dek: Cincinnati's overtime win over Tennessee produced the league's 1,098th different final score. The Titans led 36-29 with under four minutes left before the Bengals drove 81 yards to tie it.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Bears visit the Seahawks tonight at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
top.dek: Chicago brings a 5-2 record to Seattle, which is 4-3, on Monday Night Football. Watch how the Bears protect Caleb Williams and how they handle Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who has topped 100 yards in six of Seattle's first seven games.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills roll Ravens after a slow start

stories.text: Bills pull away from Ravens 36-10 to stay atop the AFC
stories.summary: Buffalo beat Baltimore 36-10 at Highmark Stadium and improved to 6-1, first in the AFC East. Josh Allen threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns and ran for another, and Tyler Bass hit a 56-yard field goal. The Bills outscored the Ravens 20-3 after halftime while Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson to a thumb injury on the first snap.

stories.text: DJ Moore shrugs off knee scare, expects to face Vikings
stories.summary: Moore hyperextended his knee on a late tackle but says he is fine and expects to be full go for the Vikings next Monday night. He had just returned from missing two games with a shoulder injury. Receiver Josh Palmer is the bigger concern after leaving in the first quarter with a right hamstring injury. ESPN reported him ruled out for the rest of the game.

stories.text: Allen breaks Jim Kelly's franchise touchdown record
stories.summary: Josh Allen's 11-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore in the fourth quarter was the 259th touchdown of his career, the most in Bills history. The old mark belonged to Jim Kelly. Allen finished 21 of 34 for 289 yards, two passing touchdowns and one interception, plus a rushing score. He was 13 of 15 for 177 yards in the second half.

stories.text: 20: Blitzes Buffalo sent at Baltimore, a season high
stories.summary: The Bills brought extra rushers on 20 snaps, more than in any game this season. Baltimore averaged 2.5 yards per play against the blitz and converted 3 of 13 third downs. Cole Bishop forced a strip sack on Tyler Huntley, and rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr recovered it.

stories.text: Bills visit Vikings on Monday night
stories.summary: Buffalo plays at Minnesota on Monday, Nov. 9 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Bills come off a Week 7 bye and a 36-10 win. Watch whether Moore and the receiver group stay healthy with Palmer hurt.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins fade after a 13-3 halftime lead

stories.text: Dolphins let a 13-3 halftime lead slip away to Patriots
stories.summary: Miami led New England 13-3 at the half, then managed only six more points in a 24-19 loss. The Patriots ran off 21 straight points in the second half. The Dolphins fell to 1-6 a week after their first win of the season.

stories.text: Brents and Proctor entered concussion protocol before game
stories.summary: Cornerback JuJu Brents and lineman Kadyn Proctor were in the concussion protocol and did not practice Thursday, coach Jeff Hafley said. Every other player on the 53-man roster was set to practice. This report predates Sunday's game, and no postgame injury update was found.

stories.text: Willis sharp early, then Miami's offense stalls
stories.summary: Malik Willis went 12 of 15 for 112 yards and a touchdown in the first half. Miami's first three possessions after halftime produced two three-and-outs and an interception. Running back Ollie Gordon was held to 69 yards on 19 carries.

stories.text: 3rd-and-20: One penalty flips the game for Miami
stories.summary: Leading 13-10 in the third quarter, Miami faced third-and-5 when Gordon drew an unsportsmanlike conduct flag for words with Robert Spillane. The penalty made it third-and-20. Willis threw incomplete, Miami punted, and New England drove 73 yards in 13 plays to take a 17-13 lead.

stories.text: Dolphins host Lions on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Miami hosts Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox. Willis said he told Gordon he was wrong after the penalty, and Hafley backed his quarterback, so locker room tone is worth watching.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Maye rallies Patriots past Miami

stories.text: Patriots storm back from 13-3 to beat Dolphins 24-19
stories.summary: New England scored 21 straight points in the second half in the rain at Hard Rock Stadium. The win moved the Patriots to 5-3 overall and 3-0 in the AFC East. It also bounced them back from a Week 7 loss to the Bears.

stories.text: Tight end Hunter Henry leaves with foot injury
stories.summary: Henry hurt his foot and left the game in the second quarter. The team had no update on his return in the sources reviewed. A.J. Brown (ankle and knee) and TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sat out, and cornerback Carlton Davis returned after three missed games.

stories.text: DeMario Douglas turns short pass into 48-yard score
stories.summary: With A.J. Brown out, Douglas caught three passes for 76 yards and a 48-yard touchdown. Kyle Williams added a 43-yard touchdown catch, and Efton Chism III had five receptions. The thin receiver group still gave Drake Maye enough in the second half.

stories.text: 158.3: Maye's second-half passer rating in Miami
stories.summary: Maye completed 9 of 10 passes for 146 yards after halftime. Patriots.com credits him with four total touchdowns on the day, passing and rushing. New England's site notes he has thrown three or more touchdown passes in five straight games, the first Patriots quarterback to do that since Tom Brady in 2007.

stories.text: Patriots host Packers on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: New England hosts Green Bay on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox, during Gronk Hall of Fame weekend. Watch Henry's status and how the receiver group holds up without Brown.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets fall to Raiders, drop third straight

stories.text: Jets lose 38-33 as Geno Smith's final throw is picked
stories.summary: New York led 23-14 at halftime but lost to Las Vegas and fell to 2-6, its third straight loss. Smith threw toward Garrett Wilson in the end zone with 14 seconds left and no timeouts, and Jeremy Chinn intercepted it. Red-zone trips that ended in field goals hurt the Jets all afternoon.

stories.text: Breece Hall misses fifth straight game with quad injury
stories.summary: Coach Aaron Glenn says Hall is close to returning but the team wants to avoid a setback. The Jets also played without defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat and edge rusher David Bailey. Bailey has a groin issue and is expected back in Week 9.

stories.text: Braelon Allen posts career-high 147 rushing yards
stories.summary: Allen carried 21 times for 147 yards and a 21-yard touchdown in the third quarter. He has topped 78 yards in each of his last four games, including two 100-yard games. Adonai Mitchell also set a career high with 142 receiving yards and a touchdown.

stories.text: 5: First-half drives, five Jets scores, still a loss
stories.summary: New York scored on all five of its first-half possessions to build a 23-14 lead. Las Vegas then outscored the Jets 15-3 in the third quarter. Kicker Sanders made four field goals, including a 31-yard kick that cut the lead to two late.

stories.text: Jets visit Chiefs on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: New York plays at Kansas City on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. The Jets face a Chiefs team that lost its last two games, per the league standings. Watch whether Hall returns and whether the red-zone issues get fixed.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Lamar Jackson needs thumb surgery, heads to IR

stories.text: Jackson headed to injured reserve after thumb injury
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson hurt his right thumb on the first snap of his return against Buffalo. Coach Jesse Minter said Jackson will have surgery and go on injured reserve, and called a season-ending result a possibility. Baltimore has now lost three straight and sits at 4-4.

stories.text: Huntley out with a toe injury, Jackson out at least four games
stories.summary: Backup Tyler Huntley hurt his toe against the Bills and has been ruled out. Jackson must miss at least four games once he goes on injured reserve, which covers Jacksonville, the Chargers, Carolina and Houston. The earliest he could return is Week 14, after the Week 13 bye.

stories.text: Undrafted rookie Fagnano gets thrown into his debut
stories.summary: Joe Fagnano made his NFL debut when both quarterbacks ahead of him went down. He finished 10 of 21 for 91 yards with one interception and a lost fumble, and he took several hits behind a line that gave up four sacks.

stories.text: 144: total yards for the Ravens in a 36-10 loss
stories.summary: Baltimore gathered just 144 yards against Buffalo. The offense allowed four sacks and 12 quarterback hits. General manager Eric DeCosta must now decide on quarterback help before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

stories.text: Ravens host Jaguars Thursday night on Prime Video
stories.summary: Baltimore hosts Jacksonville on Thursday, Nov. 5 at 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video. Watch who starts at quarterback, since Jackson and Huntley are both out and the roster could change before kickoff.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Burrow runs in OT winner in 43-36 shootout

stories.text: Bengals outlast Titans 43-36 in overtime
stories.summary: Cincinnati won its third straight game when Joe Burrow scrambled in from nine yards out in overtime. The Bengals drove 70 yards in five plays, then stopped Tennessee on downs to finish it. The win moves them to 5-2.

stories.text: Three defenders leave the Titans game hurt
stories.summary: Cornerback DJ Turner II left in the fourth quarter and did not return. Rookie defensive end Cashius Howell has a right wrist injury and was declared out, and Cedric Johnson has a left ankle injury. The team has not given timetables for any of the three.

stories.text: Tee Higgins posts 155 yards and two scores
stories.summary: Tee Higgins caught 10 passes for 155 yards and two touchdowns against Tennessee. It was the 18th 100-yard receiving game of his career. Ja'Marr Chase added 11 catches for 141 yards and a touchdown.

stories.text: 462: Burrow's passing yards in the overtime win
stories.summary: Joe Burrow went 38 of 48 for 462 yards and five touchdowns, with three interceptions, and added a rushing score. He passed Carson Palmer for fourth on the Bengals' career passing yards list at 22,925. He went 15 of 16 for 214 yards on the last three touchdown drives.

stories.text: Bengals face Falcons in Madrid on Sunday morning
stories.summary: Cincinnati plays the Falcons in Madrid, Spain on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 9:30 AM ET on NFL Network. Watch the cornerback and defensive end depth after three defenders went down against Tennessee.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns lose 27-6 and fall out of first place

stories.text: Steelers beat Browns 27-6, take AFC North lead
stories.summary: Cleveland never reached the end zone for the first time this season. The Browns fumbled on their first two possessions and Deshaun Watson went down for eight sacks. Pittsburgh took sole possession of first place at 6-2 while the Browns dropped to 5-3.

stories.text: Watson shaken up, Tytus Howard in concussion protocol
stories.summary: Watson left briefly after a high hit that drew a roughing the passer flag, and Shedeur Sanders played one series before Watson returned. Before the game, tackle Tytus Howard was in concussion protocol and did not practice, and defensive linemen Mike Hall Jr. and Mason Graham were managing lower leg injuries.

stories.text: Harold Fannin Jr. sets a career high with 154 yards
stories.summary: Fannin caught 10 passes for 154 yards, a career best, and was the Browns' top performer on offense. Watson threw for 324 yards in the loss, but Cleveland never found the end zone.

stories.text: 34: rushing yards for Cleveland against Pittsburgh
stories.summary: The Browns ran for 34 yards while Pittsburgh piled up 200 on the ground. Cleveland's defense allowed 160 rushing yards before halftime alone.

stories.text: Browns visit Saints on Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cleveland travels to New Orleans on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1:00 PM ET on CBS. Watch whether the offensive line can slow the pass rush after eight sacks, and how the run game responds against a team that gets its yards on the ground.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers win fourth straight, own the AFC North

stories.text: Steelers roll Browns 27-6 and take sole lead of the North
stories.summary: Pittsburgh won its fourth straight game and took sole possession of first place in the division at 6-2. It was the 23rd straight regular-season home win over Cleveland, and the team is 4-0 at home under Mike McCarthy. The Steelers now head into their bye week.

stories.text: Roman Wilson, Derrick Harmon still working back
stories.summary: Receiver Roman Wilson has a finger injury and was in the rehab group at practice last week for the first time. He is eligible to return in Week 10. Defensive lineman Derrick Harmon is still recovering from a foot injury, and Sebastian Joseph-Day is on injured reserve.

stories.text: Jaylen Warren runs for 143 yards on 17 carries
stories.summary: Warren tied his career high with 143 rushing yards on 17 carries and scored in the win. Rico Dowdle added 56 yards and a touchdown as Pittsburgh ran for 200 as a team.

stories.text: 8: sacks by Pittsburgh, the most in a game since 2021
stories.summary: T.J. Watt had two sacks, Patrick Queen had 1.5 and Cameron Heyward had 1.5. Pittsburgh has not allowed a second-half touchdown since Week 3 and has shut out its last two opponents after halftime.

stories.text: Bye week, then a trip to Cincinnati on NBC
stories.summary: Pittsburgh is off in Week 9. The Steelers visit the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 8:20 PM ET on NBC. Wilson is eligible to return for that game.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans use bye to reset at 2-5

stories.text: Texans trade practice for rest during bye at 2-5
stories.summary: Houston sits at 2-5 after an overtime loss to the Giants. DeMeco Ryans canceled the usual bye-week practices so players can rest their bodies and clear their heads. Coaches will spend the week self-scouting the first seven games, and practice resumes Wednesday.

stories.text: Jaylin Noel lands on IR with turf toe
stories.summary: Noel hurt his toe on a fourth-quarter kick return against the Giants, and Houston placed him on injured reserve Wednesday. A source expects him to miss the rest of the season. He led the Texans with 331 receiving yards and averaged 17.4 yards per catch. The team signed running back Emari Demercado to fill the roster spot.

stories.text: Tank Dell eases back after 22 months away
stories.summary: Dell returned in Week 7 after missing 22 months with a knee injury. He played 10 offensive snaps against the Giants and caught a 43-yard pass from C.J. Stroud. He also took over punt returns and brought one back 14 yards. The Texans are still managing his snap count.

stories.text: 188: rushing yards the Giants piled up on Houston
stories.summary: That total is the most the Texans defense has allowed on the ground this season. On offense Houston went 3 for 12 on third down and ran for just 84 yards in the same loss. The report points to weak play inside on both lines as the problem to fix during the bye.

stories.text: Texans visit the Chargers on Nov. 8
stories.summary: Houston plays at SoFi Stadium against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:05 PM ET on CBS. It is the first game of the second half of the season. Watch whether the Texans fix their interior line play against the run.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts rebuild as Taylor trade talks heat up

stories.text: Colts open rebuild and listen on Jonathan Taylor
stories.summary: Indianapolis traded guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner last week for a 2027 third-round pick, a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. ESPN reports the Colts are now willing to trade running back Jonathan Taylor and have talked with several teams. Taylor says he has not asked for a trade.

stories.text: Justin Walley's knee costs Colts a corner
stories.summary: Walley tweaked his knee against the Vikings in Week 7 and sat out all three Week 8 practices. He missed the Jaguars game. His next chance to play is Week 9 against the Cowboys.

stories.text: Taylor goes quiet in a blowout
stories.summary: Jonathan Taylor carried eight times for 23 yards against Jacksonville's top-ranked run defense. He called the 42-7 loss an old-fashioned butt whooping and said he is part of it. Entering the game he had 587 rushing yards and eight touchdowns.

stories.text: 13: losses in the Colts' last 15 games
stories.summary: Indianapolis has dropped four straight and 13 of its last 15 dating to last season. The offense gained 243 yards in the 42-7 loss at Jacksonville. Daniel Jones threw two interceptions and Anthony Richardson replaced him in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Colts host Cowboys on Nov. 8
stories.summary: Indianapolis hosts Dallas on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1:00 PM ET on Fox. Watch the quarterback decision between Jones and Richardson, and whether Taylor is still on the roster by kickoff.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars rout Colts, lead South by three games

stories.text: Jaguars blow out Colts 42-7 to stretch division lead
stories.summary: Jacksonville led 28-0 at halftime and moved to 5-2 with a three-game lead in the AFC South. Trevor Lawrence threw three touchdown passes on 10-of-14 passing for 210 yards. The Jaguars have won seven straight regular-season home games, all by 17 points or more.

stories.text: DaVon Hamilton's knee injury looked severe
stories.summary: The nose tackle was carted off in the second quarter with a right knee injury and ruled out. One report said the injury looked season-ending, though the team has not announced a diagnosis. Safety Eric Murray (elbow), end Travon Walker (ribs) and right guard Ezra Cleveland (ankle) also got hurt in the game.

stories.text: Bhayshul Tuten sets career highs against Indy
stories.summary: Tuten ran 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown, breaking three tackles on a 39-yard score. He also caught a screen for a 25-yard touchdown and finished with 55 receiving yards. Both his rushing and receiving totals were career highs.

stories.text: 183: rushing yards, a Jaguars season best
stories.summary: Jacksonville ran for 183 yards against Indianapolis, its top mark of the year. Rayuan Lane added a 92-yard interception return for a touchdown with 10 seconds left in the first half. The defense also finished with four sacks and three takeaways.

stories.text: Jaguars visit Ravens on Thursday night
stories.summary: Jacksonville plays at Baltimore on Thursday, Nov. 5, at 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video, a short week. The Jaguars then play at Tennessee on Nov. 15. Watch how the defense replaces Hamilton in the middle.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans lose 43-36 in OT after Simmons trade

stories.text: Titans fall in overtime days after trading Simmons
stories.summary: Tennessee sent All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears for two first-round picks last Thursday. The Titans then jumped out to a 13-0 lead and led 36-29 with under four minutes left. Cincinnati tied it and won 43-36 in overtime, dropping Tennessee to 1-7.

stories.text: Carnell Tate expected back after bye
stories.summary: The rookie receiver sat out the Bengals game with a shoulder injury after missing all of the week's practices. Tennessee has a Week 9 bye, and Tate is expected to return Nov. 15 against Jacksonville. He leads the team with 34 catches for 413 yards through seven games.

stories.text: Cam Ward sets a career high in yards
stories.summary: The rookie quarterback threw for 304 yards, a career best, against Cincinnati. The Titans played without Tate. The offense could not move the ball in overtime, and the final drive ended on downs.

stories.text: 1,098: unique final scores in NFL history, with 43-36 the newest
stories.summary: The Bengals' overtime win over the Titans was the league's 1,098th different final score. It was Tennessee's first scorigami since its 45-26 win over Detroit in 2020. The Titans led 36-29 with under four minutes remaining before Cincinnati marched 81 yards to tie it.

stories.text: Titans take a bye, then host Jaguars Nov. 15
stories.summary: Tennessee is off in Week 9. The Titans return Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1:00 PM ET on Fox against Jacksonville at home. Watch whether Tate is back and how the defensive line looks without Simmons.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos take AFC West lead on goal-line stand

stories.text: Broncos rally past Chiefs and take control of the AFC West
stories.summary: Denver trailed 24-13 early in the fourth quarter and won 28-24 at home. Malcolm Roach and Nik Bonitto sacked Patrick Mahomes on a replayed fourth-and-goal with 4 seconds left. The Broncos are 6-2 and sit a half-game ahead of Kansas City.

stories.text: Broncos lose two defensive backs during Chiefs win
stories.summary: Cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine hurt his ankle and left in the second quarter. Safety Brandon Jones hurt his hamstring and was ruled out at halftime. The reports I read gave no timetable for either player.

stories.text: Bo Nix finishes another comeback with two fourth-quarter scores
stories.summary: Nix completed 20 of 32 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions. He hit Nate Adkins for a 2-yard score, then found rookie Jonah Coleman for 51 yards before Coleman ran in the go-ahead touchdown. Denver scored touchdowns on both fourth-quarter drives after three straight three-and-outs in the third.

stories.text: 15: Nix's game-winning drives, most by a QB in his first three seasons
stories.summary: Nix recorded his 15th career game-winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime. That passes Dak Prescott's 14 for the most by a quarterback in his first three seasons since the 1970 merger. Denver has also won 15 one-score games over the last two seasons.

stories.text: Broncos visit Panthers Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Denver plays at Carolina in Week 9, then has its bye in Week 10. The Broncos are 10 of 48 on third down over their last four games, all wins, and that number is the thing to watch in Charlotte.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs drop second straight, fall behind Denver

stories.text: Chiefs lose second in a row after goal-line stand fails
stories.summary: Kansas City reached the Denver 1-yard line with 35 seconds left and could not score in four tries. A false start wiped out a touchdown pass to Rashee Rice, and Roach sacked Mahomes on the replay to end it. The Chiefs fell to 5-2 and now trail Denver by a half-game.

stories.text: Chiefs defensive lineman Peter Woods hurt his neck
stories.summary: Woods left in the first quarter with a neck injury, according to the AP game story. A FOX Sports takeaways piece from the same game reported no new injuries for either team, so treat his status as unconfirmed until the team updates it this week.

stories.text: Rookie Emmett Johnson leads Chiefs with 128 receiving yards
stories.summary: Johnson, a fifth-round pick from Nebraska, caught five passes for 128 yards, including a 71-yard touchdown from Mahomes. FOX Sports says that is the most receiving yards by a Chiefs running back in the Mahomes era. Kansas City is leaning on him in the passing game while it manages Kenneth Walker III's workload.

stories.text: 80-3: Mahomes' record when leading by double digits late
stories.summary: Mahomes was 80-3 in his career when his team led by 10 or more in the fourth quarter before Sunday. The Chiefs led 24-13 early in the fourth and lost 28-24. Mahomes threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions in the loss.

stories.text: Chiefs host Jets Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City returns to Arrowhead in Week 9 against a New York team that has lost three straight. Watch Butker, who missed a 54-yard field goal against Denver, and how the offense finishes drives.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders snap skid with 38-33 win over Jets

stories.text: Raiders rally past Jets 38-33 to snap a four-game skid
stories.summary: Las Vegas trailed 30-21 in the third quarter and outscored New York 17-3 the rest of the way. Matt Gay kicked a 53-yard field goal with 31 seconds left, and Jeremy Chinn intercepted Geno Smith in the end zone with 14 seconds to go. The Raiders are back to 4-4.

stories.text: Cornerback Darien Porter leaves with a groin injury
stories.summary: Porter hurt his groin on the Raiders' first defensive play and did not return. The game story gave no update on his status, so watch the practice report this week.

stories.text: Kirk Cousins accounts for four touchdowns in comeback
stories.summary: Cousins completed 19 of 26 passes for 247 yards and three touchdowns, two to Brock Bowers and one to Jalen Nailor. He also scored on a 1-yard run. Ashton Jeanty added a 45-yard screen catch that set up the go-ahead score.

stories.text: 95: Dylan Laube's kickoff return for a touchdown
stories.summary: Laube took a kickoff back 95 yards for a touchdown to give the Raiders a 14-13 lead in the first half. It was the first kickoff return touchdown in the NFL this season. Rookie Mike Washington Jr. also carried 25 times for 83 yards.

stories.text: Raiders visit 49ers Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Las Vegas plays at San Francisco in Week 9, then returns home to face Seattle in Week 10. The Raiders gave up 33 points to the Jets, so the defense has work to do against the 49ers.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Chargers fall to 0-7 with no touchdown again

stories.text: Winless Chargers fall to Rams 24-9, worst start since 2000
stories.summary: Los Angeles led 9-3 early before the Rams took over in the second half. The Chargers are 0-7, the NFL's only winless team, and have gone nine quarters without a touchdown. Jim Harbaugh said there is no quit in the locker room.

stories.text: Derwin James placed on injured reserve with hamstring injury
stories.summary: The Chargers moved safety Derwin James to injured reserve Saturday after he missed his fourth straight game. Linebacker Daiyan Henley hurt his shoulder in the first quarter and returned to the game.

stories.text: Justin Herbert throws two more interceptions in loss
stories.summary: Herbert passed for 257 yards and threw two interceptions against the Rams. He has thrown at least one interception in all seven games this season. The offense gained 295 total yards but kicked three field goals and never reached the end zone.

stories.text: 9: quarters since the Chargers last scored a touchdown
stories.summary: Los Angeles has failed to score a touchdown in two straight games, a stretch of nine quarters. Mike McDaniel's offense used two flea-flickers in the second quarter and turned them into a field goal. The Chargers' 0-7 mark is their worst start since 2000.

stories.text: Chargers host Texans Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Los Angeles returns home in Week 9 against Houston, then plays at Baltimore on Monday night in Week 10. Harbaugh called the next game the chance to respond. The first touchdown in nine quarters is the thing to watch.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys cough up 14-point lead in OT loss

stories.text: Cowboys blow a 14-point fourth-quarter lead to Arizona
stories.summary: Dallas led Arizona 24-10 in the fourth quarter and lost 33-30 in overtime at home. Backup quarterback Gardner Minshew took over for Jacoby Brissett and rallied the Cardinals, and Chad Ryland kicked the winning field goal after a three-play Dallas possession. Owner Jerry Jones called the loss an indictment of the whole show.

stories.text: Downs in concussion protocol, Ferguson hurt its ankle
stories.summary: Safety Caleb Downs left in the fourth quarter and entered the concussion protocol. Tight end Jake Ferguson went out in the third quarter with an ankle injury, and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. needs more testing on his ankle. Safety P.J. Locke also got hurt in overtime and has no status yet.

stories.text: Prescott accounts for two scores in the loss
stories.summary: Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions. He also ran seven times for 20 yards and a score, and Arizona sacked him four times. George Pickens caught two passes for 48 yards, and a 35-yard catch came back on a holding penalty.

stories.text: 467-261: Arizona's yardage edge in Dallas
stories.summary: The Cardinals outgained the Cowboys 467 yards to 261 and ran for 202 yards. Tyler Allgeier alone gained 147 yards on 11 carries, including a 63-yard touchdown. Dallas converted only 6 of 16 third downs.

stories.text: Cowboys visit the Colts on Sunday
stories.summary: Dallas plays at Indianapolis on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Cowboys then host San Francisco in Week 10. Watch how the defense handles a lead after Arizona's late rally.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants lead the NFC East coming off bye

stories.text: Giants hold the NFC East lead at the bye
stories.summary: New York sits at 4-2-1 and leads the division by two games in the win column after a 27-21 overtime win in Houston. Three different quarterbacks have won games for the Giants this season, which Giants.com says has not happened since starts were first tracked in 1950. J.J. McCarthy now runs the offense after Jaxson Dart's injury.

stories.text: Tracy lands on IR with a hamstring injury
stories.summary: Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. goes on injured reserve after hurting his hamstring against Houston. General manager Joe Schoen called it short of long-term, and Tracy will miss at least four games. The Giants signed Gregory Desrosiers from the Chargers' practice squad, and Devin Singletary moves up the depth chart.

stories.text: McCarthy throws for 252 yards in first Giants start
stories.summary: J.J. McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards in his first start for New York, a 99.1 passer rating. The Giants got him from Minnesota for a 2027 fifth-round pick. He also threw for 243 yards in relief against the Saints a week earlier.

stories.text: 124: Skattebo's career-high rushing day
stories.summary: Cam Skattebo ran 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown in Houston, a career high. He had managed 34 yards against the Saints the week before. The Giants backs combined for 188 rushing yards, and Singletary scored the 30-yard game winner.

stories.text: Giants hit Philadelphia, then host Washington
stories.summary: New York plays at Philadelphia on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. Five days later the Giants host Washington on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Giants.com notes John Harbaugh is 15-3 in games right after a bye.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles lose sixth straight to Commanders

stories.text: Eagles drop a sixth straight game in Washington
stories.summary: Washington beat Philadelphia 27-10 on Sunday night and shut the Eagles out over the final three quarters. The Eagles led 10-0 early and then watched the game slip away. They are 2-6 and own the league's second-longest active losing streak.

stories.text: Hurts out for the season with blood clots in lungs
stories.summary: Jalen Hurts is likely done for the year after doctors found blood clots in his lungs. Tanner McKee has started in his place. Hurts has stayed in touch with McKee as a resource.

stories.text: Barkley gets 30 yards on 13 carries
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley scored on a 3-yard run early, but Washington stacked the box and held him to 30 rushing yards on 13 carries. He added a 24-yard catch. Philadelphia had little else working without Hurts.

stories.text: 204: rushing yards Dallas ran for on Philly
stories.summary: The Eagles allowed 204 rushing yards in their 38-21 Monday night loss to Dallas, and their run defense ranks 27th in the league. Washington then sacked McKee four times with nine quarterback hits on Sunday. The trenches have been the weak point during the skid.

stories.text: Eagles host the Giants before a Week 10 bye
stories.summary: Philadelphia hosts the 4-2-1 Giants on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Eagles then take their Week 10 bye. The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10, so watch which veterans move.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders end skid, pass Eagles in East

stories.text: Commanders beat the Eagles for their first win in a month
stories.summary: Washington beat Philadelphia 27-10 on Sunday night, its first win since Sept. 27 against Seattle. The Commanders trailed 10-0 early and finished the game on a 27-0 run. They moved past the Eagles in the NFC East standings.

stories.text: McLaurin out for the year with a knee injury
stories.summary: Wide receiver Terry McLaurin is done for the season with a knee injury. Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt, the team's leading rusher with 239 yards, is on injured reserve. Defensive tackles Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw were inactive against Philadelphia.

stories.text: Daniels throws for 217 yards with no turnovers
stories.summary: Jayden Daniels completed 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions. He also scrambled for 23 yards. Treylon Burks led the receivers with three catches for 81 yards.

stories.text: 27: unanswered points on the Eagles
stories.summary: Washington scored the final 27 points after falling behind 10-0. The defense sacked Tanner McKee four times and hit him nine times. Drew Stevens kicked four field goals, from 56, 39, 25 and 42 yards.

stories.text: Commanders host the Rams, then visit the Giants
stories.summary: Washington hosts the 4-4 Rams on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Commanders then visit the Giants on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. They trail New York by two games in the division.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears play Seattle on Monday night at 5-2

stories.text: Bears carry a 5-2 record into Monday night in Seattle
stories.summary: Chicago plays the second of three straight primetime games tonight at Lumen Field. The Bears are coming off a win over New England, and fans want to see trade acquisition Jeffery Simmons make his debut. Whether he plays is not confirmed.

stories.text: Cole Kmet heads to injured reserve with a knee injury
stories.summary: Coach Ben Johnson said the tight end will go on injured reserve after he left the Patriots game with a knee injury. Patrick Finley of the Chicago Sun-Times reported Kmet is on track to miss the rest of the season. Sam Roush should see more snaps, and the Bears figure to add a tight end.

stories.text: Caleb Williams tops 300 yards with no interceptions
stories.summary: Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions in the 30-24 win over New England. He ran five times for 18 yards and completed all five throws on the move. It was his second straight 300-yard game since he returned from a hamstring injury.

stories.text: 2018: Last time a Bears QB threw 300 in back-to-back games
stories.summary: Williams is the first Bears quarterback with consecutive 300-yard passing games since Mitchell Trubisky in 2018. He also tied Sid Luckman for second in team history with his 13th game of multiple touchdown passes and no interception. Jay Cutler leads that list with 18.

stories.text: Bears at Seahawks tonight, 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Chicago visits Seattle (4-3) on Monday Night Football. Watch how the Bears protect Williams and how they handle receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who has 100 yards in six of Seattle's first seven games. Tampa Bay comes to Soldier Field on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions end Vikings' unbeaten run, 19-15

stories.text: Lions end the Vikings' unbeaten run with a 19-15 win
stories.summary: Jared Goff found Jameson Williams in the back of the end zone to cap a drive that started behind 15-12. Detroit moved to 5-2 and 2-0 in the division. The defense then forced a three-and-out and the offense ran out the clock.

stories.text: Lions leave Minnesota game with a long injury list
stories.summary: Linebacker Jack Campbell hurt his neck on a tackle and went to a local hospital for evaluation. Center Cade Mays (ankle), edge DJ Wonnum and safety Brian Branch were ruled out during the game, and linebacker Jimmy Rolder (hamstring) did not return. Cornerback D.J. Reed hurt his hip in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs runs for 153 yards and the go-ahead score
stories.summary: Gibbs broke a 30-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter, his longest of the season and his 10th touchdown. He joins Barry Sanders as the only Lions players with 10 touchdowns in four straight seasons. Goff added 176 yards passing and extended his touchdown streak to 29 games.

stories.text: 230: Rushing yards for Detroit against Minnesota
stories.summary: The Lions ran for 230 yards while their defense allowed 266 total yards and 15 points, both season lows. Minnesota went 3-of-10 on third down, and Detroit sacked Kyler Murray three times.

stories.text: Lions at Dolphins, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Detroit travels to Miami on Sunday, Nov. 8. Watch the injury report for Campbell, Mays, Wonnum, Branch and Reed. The Lions host New England the following week.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Love throws three TDs as Packers beat Carolina

stories.text: Packers beat Carolina 27-19 on Thursday night
stories.summary: Green Bay improved to 5-3 with a win at Lambeau Field. Jordan Love threw three touchdown passes, and the defense sacked Bryce Young six times. The Packers now turn to a road game at New England.

stories.text: Christian Watson plays on with a broken rib
stories.summary: Watson broke a rib and was checked for internal bleeding. A CT scan showed none, and he returned to the game. Tight end Josh Whyle was evaluated for a concussion in the first half, and the outcome was not stated.

stories.text: Jordan Love goes 30-of-41 for 288 yards and three scores
stories.summary: Love threw touchdowns to Tucker Kraft (12 yards), Matthew Golden (24 yards) and Josh Jacobs (4 yards). He also threw one interception. Watson caught eight passes for 113 yards, including a 53-yarder that set up a Jacobs touchdown.

stories.text: 4: Packers with six or more catches in one game
stories.summary: Watson (8), Golden (7), Kraft (6) and Jacobs (6) all reached six catches, only the third time in franchise history. The earlier games came in 2007 and 1993. The run game managed 66 yards on 26 carries.

stories.text: Packers at Patriots, Sunday 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Green Bay visits New England on Sunday, Nov. 8. Watch whether the run game improves after a 39-yard night from Jacobs. Minnesota visits Lambeau Field the following week.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Vikings lose first game, offense stalls in Detroit

stories.text: Vikings fall 19-15 to Detroit for their first loss
stories.summary: Minnesota dropped to 6-1 as its offense stalled again. The defense tired in the second half, and Detroit scored 13 points after halftime. Coach Kevin O'Connell called it the team's first real adversity.

stories.text: Kyler Murray finishes with hamstring tightness
stories.summary: Murray said the tightness came in the fourth quarter and did not limit him much. The Vikings will look at it. The report listed no other new Minnesota injuries.

stories.text: Justin Jefferson gets 5 catches for 33 yards, one score
stories.summary: Jefferson made a one-handed, 1-yard touchdown catch on nine targets. Three throws sailed over his head, and D.J. Reed intercepted one just before halftime. O'Connell and Murray both said the Vikings must find ways to get him the ball.

stories.text: 14: Carries for Vikings running backs, a season low
stories.summary: Murray dropped back on 33 of Minnesota's 50 offensive plays, and O'Connell said the team needs better run and pass balance. The Vikings also went 3-of-10 on third down and Will Reichard missed a 57-yard field goal.

stories.text: Vikings host Bills, Monday Nov. 9, 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Minnesota gets a Monday night home game against Buffalo, then visits Green Bay on Nov. 15. Watch whether O'Connell changes the run and pass mix after the Detroit loss.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Penix throws four picks in 16-0 loss

stories.text: Falcons get shut out in Tampa as Penix throws four interceptions
stories.summary: Atlanta lost 16-0 at Tampa Bay on Sunday and fell to 3-5, a week after beating San Francisco. Michael Penix Jr. went 8 of 24 for 125 yards with four interceptions, two of them to Alex Anzalone in the first quarter. Coach Kevin Stefanski said the Bucs outplayed and outcoached his team.

stories.text: Pearce expected back for Madrid game
stories.summary: Edge rusher James Pearce Jr. is due to return next week ahead of the Bengals game. Penix looked fully recovered from his ACL tear in the loss, and the Falcons reported no new injuries from the game. Atlanta's pass rush needs the help.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson stuck in a game the Falcons could not run
stories.summary: Robinson carried 19 times for 76 yards against Tampa Bay and entered the day with 704 rushing yards and four touchdowns. Atlanta ran for just 99 yards as a team while the Bucs piled up 324. Robinson said the Falcons cannot keep turning the ball over.

stories.text: 0-for-12: Atlanta's third-down day in Tampa
stories.summary: The Falcons did not convert a single one of their 12 third downs. They also gained 4 yards on 10 plays that needed 2 yards or fewer on third or fourth down. Penix finished with a career-low minus-0.87 total EPA.

stories.text: Falcons face Bengals in Madrid on Sunday morning
stories.summary: Atlanta plays Cincinnati on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network at Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid. The Falcons are one game back of the NFC South lead in the loss column. Watch whether Penix bounces back and whether the left tackle spot holds up.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Six sacks sink Panthers at Lambeau

stories.text: Panthers fall 27-19 at Green Bay as pressure swamps Young
stories.summary: Carolina lost Thursday night at Lambeau Field and dropped to 3-4. Green Bay led 27-10 before Bryce Young led a late push, including a 26-yard fourth-down touchdown to Jalen Coker. A two-point try failed with 5:37 left,.

stories.text: Moton done for the year, secondary thinning out
stories.summary: Right tackle Taylor Moton will have season-ending ankle surgery after leaving the Oct. 25 loss to Tampa Bay with a fractured fibula and ligament damage. First-round pick Monroe Freeling moves to right tackle. Cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are on injured reserve, and Akayleb Evans missed Thursday with triceps and knee injuries.

stories.text: Hubbard carries the Carolina offense in Green Bay
stories.summary: Chuba Hubbard ran 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown. He also caught 7 of 8 targets for 38 yards. Hubbard averaged 3.7 yards per carry and the Panthers could not keep pace.

stories.text: 6: times Green Bay sacked Bryce Young
stories.summary: Young went 23 of 41 for 209 yards with one touchdown and one interception while taking six sacks. Six different Packers defenders got to him. Carolina has now lost two straight with a depleted offensive line.

stories.text: Panthers host Broncos Sunday at Bank of America Stadium
stories.summary: Carolina plays Denver on Sunday, Nov. 8 on CBS at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte. Denver comes in 5-2. Watch how a patched offensive line handles the Broncos' pass rush.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints use bye to evaluate everything

stories.text: Saints spend bye week on self-scouting at 2-5
stories.summary: Coach Kellen Moore called the bye a self-scout week and said the team would evaluate everything. He said he will focus heavily on finding ways to score points. New Orleans sits last in the NFC South heading into a Nov. 8 home game against Cleveland.

stories.text: Tyson could debut against Browns after hamstring recovery
stories.summary: Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson has not played this season because of a right hamstring strain. General manager Mickey Loomis said he is getting closer, and the bye gives him more time. A debut on Nov. 8 against Cleveland is possible if he returns to practice after the bye.

stories.text: Shough produces through the mess in New Orleans
stories.summary: Tyler Shough has completed 67 percent of his passes for 1,721 yards and 13 touchdowns. He has also thrown six interceptions and lost three fumbles while playing through a left hand injury. New Orleans has trailed in every game this season.

stories.text: 13: Saints giveaways through seven games
stories.summary: New Orleans has 13 turnovers and a minus-4 margin, per ESPN data cited by Athlon. The Saints have fumbled 11 times and lost seven. Shough has six interceptions and has been sacked 15 times.

stories.text: Saints host Browns at the Superdome after the bye
stories.summary: New Orleans plays Cleveland on Sunday, Nov. 8 at noon CT (1 p.m. ET) on CBS at the Caesars Superdome. Carolina visits the next Sunday. Watch whether Tyson and the offense get a lift from the extra week.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs win without completing a pass

stories.text: Bucs beat Falcons 16-0 without a single completed pass
stories.summary: Tampa Bay won its second straight at 3-5 behind a franchise-record rushing day. Baker Mayfield went 0 for 3, making Tampa the first team since the 1974 Bills to win without completing a pass. The defense forced four turnovers, led by two Alex Anzalone interceptions in the first quarter.

stories.text: Egbuka out again, Winfield back from rib fracture
stories.summary: Receiver Emeka Egbuka was ruled out and missed a second straight game. Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. returned after missing three games with a rib fracture. Mayfield has only 14 pass attempts during the winning streak, which raises questions about his recently healed thumb.

stories.text: Bucky Irving runs for a career-high 170 yards
stories.summary: Irving carried 27 times for 170 yards and a 4-yard touchdown, both career bests. His 46-yard run set up the Bucs' 90-yard scoring drive. Kenny Gainwell added 140 yards of his own.

stories.text: 324: Tampa Bay's rushing yards, a franchise record
stories.summary: The Bucs outran Atlanta 324 to 99 and broke the old team record of 283. Irving and Gainwell both cleared 100 yards. Sources vary slightly, with figures between 322 and 325, but NFL.com and SI both report 324.

stories.text: Bucs head to Chicago for Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Tampa Bay plays at the Bears on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC at Soldier Field. The Bucs are 3-5 and chasing the NFC South lead. Watch whether Mayfield throws more than three passes.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Minshew rallies Cardinals past Cowboys in OT

stories.text: Minshew replaces Brissett, Cardinals win in overtime
stories.summary: Arizona trailed Dallas 17-3 when Mike LaFleur pulled Jacoby Brissett for Gardner Minshew with 95 seconds left in the third quarter. Minshew threw the tying touchdown to Michael Wilson with six seconds left, and Chad Ryland won it from 42 yards in overtime, 33-30. LaFleur would not name a starter for Sunday, though a source told ESPN that Minshew is expected to keep the job.

stories.text: Cardinals lose four players in Dallas
stories.summary: Running back Jeremiyah Love left in the first half with his third ankle injury of the season. Bam Knight suffered a concussion, which left Tyler Allgeier as the only healthy back. Receiver Kendrick Bourne left on crutches with an ankle injury and rookie left tackle Jayden Williams hurt a knee. Wilson played through two broken ribs.

stories.text: Allgeier runs for 147 yards on 11 carries
stories.summary: Tyler Allgeier ripped off a 63-yard touchdown run on Minshew's second snap and finished with 147 yards on 11 carries. He also caught five passes for 44 yards and a touchdown. With the other backs hurt, he carried the backfield down the stretch.

stories.text: 467: Arizona outgained Dallas by 206 yards
stories.summary: The Cardinals piled up 467 total yards to the Cowboys' 261, and Minshew went 17 of 23 for 188 yards and three touchdowns after he entered. Arizona scored touchdowns on four straight possessions with him at quarterback. Dallas fell to 3-5, the same record as Arizona.

stories.text: At Seattle, Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Arizona travels to face the Seahawks on Sunday, November 8, at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. Watch whether Minshew starts and how the Cardinals line up at running back and left tackle after Sunday's injuries.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams reach .500 with first back-to-back wins

stories.text: Rams beat winless Chargers, reach .500
stories.summary: Los Angeles had no first down until the final two minutes of the first half, then scored 24 points to beat the Chargers 24-9. It was the Rams' first back-to-back win of the season and moved them to 4-4. The Chargers fell to 0-7, their worst start since 2000.

stories.text: Two Rams cornerbacks hurt in the second half
stories.summary: Jaylen Watson hurt his shoulder early in the second half and did not return. He missed a game last month with a dislocated shoulder. Trent McDuffie hurt his back in his first game after a two-game groin absence and finished on the sideline. Myles Garrett has missed time since Week 1 with a knee injury, and Yahoo reported he could return to practice this week.

stories.text: Corum gains 73 yards and scores for Rams
stories.summary: Blake Corum carried 11 times for 73 yards and opened the second half with a 23-yard touchdown run. The Rams had 10 rushing yards at halftime and finished with 129. Kyren Williams added 56 yards on 16 carries and a short touchdown.

stories.text: 5: straight drives without a first down
stories.summary: The Rams opened with five drives and no first down, the first time that has happened in Sean McVay's career. Matthew Stafford then threw 17 of 25 for 157 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Puka Nacua caught 11 passes for 80 yards.

stories.text: At Washington, Sunday, 1:00 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Rams visit the Commanders on Sunday, November 8, at 1:00 PM ET on Fox. Watch the cornerback depth with Watson and McDuffie both banged up. Arizona follows in Week 10.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers use bye week to get healthy

stories.text: 49ers rest after four-turnover loss to Falcons
stories.summary: San Francisco lost 29-20 at Atlanta in Week 7, its first loss, and went into the bye at 6-1. Kyle Shanahan said it is hard to win with four turnovers to zero. The 49ers host the Raiders on November 8, and the trade deadline falls on November 10.

stories.text: Bosa, Evans and Samuel eye post-bye returns
stories.summary: Christian McCaffrey has a mild hamstring strain and Shanahan is optimistic he will play Week 9. Nick Bosa (calf) has missed five straight games. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, Marques Sigle, Luke Gifford, Garret Wallow and C.J. West all have a chance to return, but Shanahan said none are guaranteed.

stories.text: Kaelon Black scores first career touchdown
stories.summary: Running back Kaelon Black broke a 30-yard touchdown run against Atlanta, his first in the NFL. Shanahan also praised receiver Christian Kirk, who made his season debut despite having no catches.

stories.text: 4: turnovers for San Francisco, zero for Atlanta
stories.summary: The 49ers gave the ball away four times while the Falcons never did. Shanahan went for it on fourth and 10 rather than kick a 41-yard field goal after a touchdown was overturned.

stories.text: Vs. Las Vegas, Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: The 49ers host the Raiders at Levi's Stadium on Sunday, November 8, at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. Shanahan speaks to reporters Wednesday and Friday. Watch how many of the injured receivers and linemen are cleared.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks add Nelson, host Bears on MNF

stories.text: Seahawks trade for guard Quenton Nelson
stories.summary: Seattle sent Indianapolis a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick for the eight-time Pro Bowl guard. Nelson is 30 and in the last year of his contract. To clear a roster spot, the Seahawks waived guard Christian Haynes. Nelson is expected to start at left guard tonight.

stories.text: Cross and Shaheed out against Chicago
stories.summary: Left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) and receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) will miss tonight's game, and Josh Jones starts at left tackle. Edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) is doubtful. Running back Zach Charbonnet makes his 2026 debut after an ACL tear and Jadarian Price returned from injured reserve.

stories.text: Emanuel Wilson posts first 100-yard game
stories.summary: Emanuel Wilson ran for exactly 100 yards against Kansas City, the first 100-yard rushing game by a Seattle back this season. He has started the last four games. Seattle expects Charbonnet or Price back, but Wilson is likely to keep getting carries.

stories.text: 7: straight opponents held under 180 passing yards
stories.summary: Seattle has held each of its first seven opponents under 180 passing yards, the longest such streak in the NFL since 1984. The defense allows the fewest yards in the league and 17.9 points per game. Caleb Williams is the next test.

stories.text: Vs. Chicago, tonight, 8:15 PM ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Seattle hosts the Bears on Monday Night Football at Lumen Field, with kickoff at 8:15 PM ET on ESPN. Chicago leads the NFL in rushing attempts and yards, so Seattle's run defense gets the first test. Arizona visits Sunday.
